label: TP
reason: User-supplied header value flows via URL decode into str, then through encodeForHTML which returns HTML-encoded content. The encoded string is concatenated directly into the response writer println call. Since ESAPI.encodeForHTML produces HTML entities rather than breaking out of HTML context within JavaScript attributes (the surrounding literal strings provide no attribute boundaries), the output remains executable JavaScript in the browser context, constituting a genuine XSS.

evidence.note: Header param decoded and passed to doSomething, then used in unescaped concatenation into response print
